sources.claim: PCM block alignment derives from channels and sample width; average bytes from rate and alignment; cbSize is ignored for PCM. The source destination-low-word cbSize must remain in its record.
8-bit PCM is unsigned with midpoint128;16-bit PCM is signed with midpoint0. Stereo is left/right interleaved and16-bit words are little endian.
DirectSound volume attenuation uses hundredths of dB, range-10000 through0, with no amplification. This does not establish device error retention or exact DSP rounding.
DirectSound pan attenuates one channel, leaving the other at full level; its attenuation combines with volume. Apple pan range alone is insufficient to prove an equivalent mapping.
AVAudioEngine can render manually; installed header supplies exact ordering and output-buffer contracts used by the proposed offline test.
Manual rendering block exists; no block or engine was executed here.
DirectSound loading and playback use secondary-buffer Lock and Play; original EXE, not this tutorial, determines NTSD call order.
WAVEFORMATEX describes mono/stereo8/16-bit PCM; support at a particular device remains a separate question.

design.rawPCM: Retain original interleaved bytes/masks separately from the platform PCM buffer. Fully known8-bit samples map to Float32(sample-128)/128;16-bit signed samples to Float32(sample)/32768. This exact representation mapping is Native design, not a claim about Windows DSP. Preserve source rate and channel order.
design.ownership: Use the existing Native resource identity pool; no host/source pointer tokens or path-based deduplication. Shared owner retained by fulfilled exchange receipts.
design.offline: Configure manual rendering before any mixer/input/output node access; no physical output or microphone. Use the same native rate/channel count to avoid claiming resampling equivalence. Observe status and actual frameLength; never infer zero samples from a short render.
design.excluded: Music WMA/graph notifications, DirectSound pan/volume mapping, runtime sound-command scheduling, hardware output/latency/mixing and Windows reference still open.
